subject.title: feat(memory-lancedb): scope memory_recall and memory_forget in a shared store

question: Should memory-lancedb expose caller-defined opaque scopes now, even though automatic recall has no trusted active-scope signal and scoped rows are therefore excluded from automatic injection?
rationale: The implementation can mechanically partition rows, but code review cannot determine whether caller-owned scope keys and global-only automatic recall are the intended long-term product semantics.

options.title: Approve the partition primitive
options.body: Accept caller-defined scope as a non-security partition after fixing the one-pass upgrade path and keeping the limitations explicit in docs.

options.title: Require trusted context binding
options.body: Hold the PR until scope is derived or validated against an active session, channel, or speaker identity and automatic recall can target it.

options.title: Defer scoped memory
options.body: Pause this PR until the broader scoped auto-recall design is ready, avoiding a partially usable public tool and storage contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the partition primitive
recommendation.body: Accept caller-defined scope as a non-security partition after fixing the one-pass upgrade path and keeping the limitations explicit in docs.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged per-agent isolation and doctor work defines the closest existing ownership and migration contract for this decision.
